pages.text: Your ancestors lived in trees, and your arms remember.$(br2)When something large wants to eat you, height is an answer. When nothing does, height is still a good place to think. Get into the habit of climbing.

Walk into a trunk and hold $(k:jump) to climb. Hold $(k:sneak) to let yourself down, or hold nothing and simply cling.$(br2)Branches do not stop a climber. Come out through the top and you can rest on the leaves; look down and $(k:sneak) to climb back in.

Most things that hunt on the ground cannot follow you up. They will look, and circle, and leave.$(br2)Pale, soft wood is another matter. Rotten trees do not always hold a climber's weight, and the ground is a long way down.
Any wall will take your weight for a little way. Push into it with $(k:jump) held and you can haul yourself about four blocks up - out of a pit, or up a low bank. No further.
